finding: With legacyCloud=false set via the CLUSTERPROP API, MIGRATE fails because OverseerCollectionProcessor.migrateKey sends a raw core-admin CREATE for the temp collection's replica2 on the target leader node without coreNodeName, which CoreAdminHandler.handleCreateAction:563 rejects ('non legacy mode coreNodeName missing').
same_root_cause: Same defect. In the buggy tree, OverseerCollectionProcessor.java:1897-1905 (migrateKey) builds a CoreAdminAction.CREATE with only name/collection/shard and sends it via sendShardRequest to the target leader, with no clusterstate registration and no coreNodeName; the validate log shows exactly that request (name=split_shard2_temp_shard1_shard1_replica2, no coreNodeName) rejected at CoreAdminHandler.java:563. The fix hunk @@ -1894,15 +1895,25 @@ replaces this raw CREATE with addReplica(...) using ADDREPLICA props, which registers the replica and passes coreNodeName.
realistic: Yes. The test is MigrateRouteKeyTest's mini SolrCloud cluster with legacyCloud=false set through the supported Collections API CLUSTERPROP call (the same trigger the fix's own test change adds), then ordinary indexing, CREATE collection and MIGRATE calls. No reflection, mocks or fabricated arguments; the only test file is new and production sources are unmodified.
fixed_version: On the buggy tree plus the fix, all 4 runs no longer hit the check; the target node's CREATE now carries coreNodeName=core_node2 and succeeds, and MIGRATE completes (the test fails only on its own assertion 'MIGRATE unexpectedly succeeded in legacyCloud=false mode'), so the consequence goes away.
reason: The agent's failing execution is exactly SOLR-6197: MIGRATE with legacyCloud=false creates the temporary collection's extra replica via core-admin CREATE without coreNodeName, and CoreAdminHandler rejects it, so the migration fails. The trigger is a valid cluster property set through the public API, the consequence (MIGRATE fails) matches the JIRA, and the fix removes the failure.
